scenario.title: Crete - Evacuation
intro.text:
CRETE - EVACUATION - 28 MAY 1941

Sphakia, Crete

The withdrawal from Crete, the evacuation to Egypt was ordered - the island is not to hold! Move to the south coast of the island and board the waiting vessels!

GOAL Retreat 12 ground units (in sea transport) via Exit Points!

NOTE Due to the short time between the missions at HQ no new units can be recruited!
player.speaker: Commander
line.reaction-10-0-briliant.speaker: Major Edward Hale
line.reaction-10-0-briliant.text: The airborne lodgement failed to become a secure bridgehead. Crete still stands, and the formation can move directly to the rebuilding army in Egypt.
line.reaction-10-1-victory-tactical.text: Enough of western Crete held to keep the defence coherent, but the airfields are becoming roads for the enemy. The argument has changed from reinforcement to evacuation.
line.reaction-10-2-lose.speaker: Petros Manesis
line.reaction-10-2-lose.text: The Cretan positions collapsed into separate fights. Ships and mountain tracks are now the only plan shared by the survivors.
line.callback-0.speaker: Major Edward Hale
line.callback-0.text: You committed early to Hill 107. Every later report measures the defence from that height, including the roads the reserve could no longer cover.
line.callback-1.speaker: Eleni Markou
line.callback-1.text: You kept the Cretan reserve moving between the docks and Aghya. More roads stayed open, though every officer on Hill 107 remembers the companies he did not receive.
line.callback-2.speaker: Major Edward Hale
line.callback-2.text: The Thermopylae anti-aircraft section remained together. On Crete it finally received more aircraft than anyone had wanted it to see.
line.callback-3.speaker: Dimitris Laskaris
line.callback-3.text: The Thermopylae section was broken up, but its observers taught every battalion to look upward before the first transport appeared.
line.scene-0.speaker: Major Edward Hale
line.scene-0.text: The naval signal promises one night and two beaches. It does not promise that a ship which leaves full will come back.
line.scene-1.speaker: Eleni Markou
line.scene-1.text: The field hospital reaches Sougia tomorrow afternoon if the road holds. I have stopped telling the wounded what time the fleet sails.
line.scene-2.speaker: Petros Manesis
line.scene-2.text: The formed column can make tonight's loading. Wait for the hospital and we ask the rear guard to fight through another daylight.
line.decision.speaker: Petros Manesis
line.decision.text: Commander: meet the fleet with the units already formed, or hold Sougia and bring down everyone we can still move?
line.decision.choice.follow-the-naval-cl: Form one fast column and meet the fleet's loading schedule.
Fully refuel and rearm the core and give transport and reconnaissance 15 experience.
line.decision.choice.bring-out-the-hospi: Hold Sougia and bring the hospital and stragglers down first.
Spend 75 prestige, restore the core to at least nine strength, and fully refuel it.
line.choice-a-0.speaker: Eleni Markou
line.choice-a-0.text: Give me the names of the rear guard before you give Hale the loading numbers. I will not let the missing become 'stragglers' in the first report.
line.choice-a-1.speaker: Major Edward Hale
line.choice-a-1.text: Each unit gets a beach and a final time. The column moves now. Anyone who misses his place does not stop the one behind him.
line.choice-b-0.speaker: Major Edward Hale
line.choice-b-0.text: One more daylight may cost the rear guard and the ships. I cannot improve that arithmetic for you.
line.choice-b-1.speaker: Eleni Markou
line.choice-b-1.text: The hospital starts now. The rear guard gets the true sailing time, not a comforting rumour. If the last ship turns away, they will know before we do.
